newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner cable to carry Fox news - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner cable to carry Fox news - NYT.

text.p: The Time Warner cable system has agreed to carry News Corp's 24-hour Fox news channel, The New York Times reported Wednesday.
The newspaper said the agreement, whose details were still being negotiated late Tuesday, would end nearly a year of bitter legal and political battles.

The paper cited "executives close to the negotiations" who said the deal would be the cornerstone of a larger pact that would give News Corp's Rupert Murdoch access to 65 percent of the systems Time Warner operates across the country.
Time Warner in turn would gain access to a vast network of international satellite television systems that Murdoch has assembled in Latin America, China and elsewhere, the article said.

Under the agreement, New York's Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, who earlier tried to intervene on Murdoch's behalf, would turn over one of the five cable channels the city now controls for educational programming to Time Warner, which would then provide that channel to the Fox news channel, the paper said.
Later, The Times said, the city would be reimbursed with another newly created Time Warner cable channel as part of a 12-channel expansion of the company's New York City system.
The deal caps the battle between Murdoch and Ted Turner, whose Cable News Network was acquired by Time Warner a year ago, and who is now vice chairman of Time Warner, the paper said.

Time Warner had said it did not have enough space on its cable system to accomodate the Fox network, but Fox executives accused Time Warner of trying to protect CNN from competition, the article said.
